note: Commitments that are judged on whether something was delivered, rather than on a running data series. Each was checked against the official page listed on the date shown. Items that could not be confirmed against an official source are held in 'pending' and are not published.

items.title: Cut student debt by 20%
items.commitment: Cut every student loan (HELP) debt by 20%.
items.reason: The law passed in 2025 and the cut has been applied to student loan accounts.

sources.label: Department of Education: HELP debt reduction

items.title: $25 cap on PBS medicines
items.commitment: Cut the maximum price of a PBS prescription from $31.60 to $25.
items.reason: The $25 maximum has applied since 1 January 2026.

items.title: A tax cut for every taxpayer
items.commitment: Income tax cuts for every taxpayer from 1 July 2024, with the lowest rate cut again to 15% from 1 July 2026.
items.reason: Both rounds were legislated and have started. Note: the 2024 cuts replaced the ‘Stage 3’ cuts the government had promised in 2022 to keep unchanged, so that earlier promise was not kept in its original form.

sources.label: ATO: tax rates for Australian residents

items.title: 137 Medicare Urgent Care Clinics
items.commitment: Open 50 Medicare Urgent Care Clinics, then a further 87, for 137 in total.
items.reason: The government reports that all 137 promised clinics are open.

sources.label: Prime Minister: all Medicare Urgent Care Clinics delivered
Department of Health: about the clinics

items.title: 5% deposits for all first home buyers
items.commitment: Let every first home buyer purchase with a 5% deposit, with no caps on places or income.
items.reason: The expanded scheme is in place and started earlier than first promised.

items.title: Free TAFE made permanent
items.commitment: Make Free TAFE a permanent part of the training system.
items.reason: The Free TAFE Act 2025 is law.

items.title: 3 Day Guarantee for child care
items.commitment: Guarantee every eligible family at least three days a week of subsidised child care, whatever their work hours.
items.reason: Since January 2026 all eligible families get at least 72 hours of subsidised care a fortnight.

items.title: 26 weeks of paid parental leave
items.commitment: Extend government-paid parental leave to 26 weeks by July 2026, and pay superannuation on it.
items.reason: For babies born or adopted from 1 July 2026, Parental Leave Pay is 130 days (26 weeks), and superannuation is paid on it.

sources.label: Services Australia: Paid Parental Leave changes

items.title: A National Anti-Corruption Commission
items.commitment: Legislate a National Anti-Corruption Commission by the end of 2022.
items.reason: The law passed in December 2022 and the Commission began work on 1 July 2023.

items.title: Social media minimum age of 16
items.commitment: Require social media platforms to keep under-16s from holding accounts.
items.reason: The requirement took effect on 10 December 2025. Whether it is working well is a separate, contested question.

sources.label: eSafety Commissioner: social media age restrictions

items.title: A referendum on the Voice
items.commitment: Hold a referendum in the first term on an Indigenous Voice to Parliament.
items.reason: The referendum was held on 14 October 2023. Voters rejected the proposal, so the Voice itself was not established.

items.title: 82% renewable electricity by 2030
items.commitment: Lift renewables to 82% of electricity in the national grid by 2030.
items.reason: Renewables supplied 39.5% of all electricity generated in 2025 (the grid-only share is a little higher). The share would need to roughly double in five years.
